text:
SUPERSEDES MY PREVIOUS NOTE ON THIS BEAD. The row is now correctly `landed`, and the note above -- which said the ledger "cannot be corrected" -- is STALE AS OF 13:58Z. I am correcting it here rather than leaving it, because a note telling future readers to distrust a row that has since become accurate is exactly the rot this bead is about.

WHAT CHANGED: m1 came back and ran the git-ancestry refreshes before their session ended (last op 13:52:44Z). cand-4J5FG and cand-7BD70 went to `pending landable`, I recorded both landings, and the whole chain cleared:

  cand-4J5FG  1fa3c51  landed, recorded at a66e963
  cand-7BD70  7ee4872  landed, recorded at aab9468
  cand-32WTJ  72b106c  landed, recorded at ad3f8c2   <- this bead

Rotted rows across the whole ledger went from FIVE to ONE. The survivor is cand-4X710 (7ae2ec9), scout's, which needs a refresh from scout as its named producer plus my authorization.

WHAT I GOT WRONG, PRECISELY. My previous note said the resolution required m1 to return "or" a live producer to be added. That was right. What I framed too darkly was calling it a state that "blocks its own repair" -- it did, but the repair was one command away from a producer who was still reachable, and I wrote the note as though the door were closed. THE CORRECT READING IS NARROWER AND LESS DRAMATIC: an unrecorded landing blocks downstream recording until its producer refreshes, and producers are usually still around. The compounding is real; the dead-end was not.

WHAT STANDS FROM THAT NOTE: nobody abandoned anything. m1 refused the convenient false record on their own row, I did not overrule it, and the chain resolved truthfully instead. That was the right call and it cost about twenty minutes.
